applicability_rule: APPLICABLE to all Tested Code, unconditionally -- 'The Tested code MUST behave as described in the documentation provided for [Q] Document Contract Logic, and [Q] Document System Architecture' has no restrictive clause, and a manual re-read of the predicate finds no hidden restriction either (unlike req-1-eip155-chainid/req-2-overflow-underflow): every contract either has documentation to compare against or doesn't, and both cases are meaningful outcomes for THIS requirement rather than reasons it wouldn't apply.

derivation_log_entry.basis_classification_rationale: Unconditioned subject, predicate re-read confirms no embedded restriction (checked specifically because of AR-001's warning).
derivation_log_entry.derivation_method: manual re-read of full normative_text against AR-001's warning

cross_reference_note: Important distinction for L7: APPLICABILITY (always yes) is separate from ASSESSABILITY. If the referenced documentation requirements (req-3-documented, req-3-document-system) are themselves unmet -- i.e. no documentation exists to compare code against -- the correct conformance state for THIS requirement is likely INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, not NOT_APPLICABLE. Conflating 'nothing to compare against' with 'doesn't apply' would be exactly the applicability/conformance fusion error the plan's Rev. 2 revision was designed to prevent.
